To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The migration inhibition factor (a T cell product) and antigen-induced proliferation (another T cell product) are not always produced by the same cells in the same animals.

a dissociation between MIP production and antigen-induced cell proliferation is observed in LNC response to the same T cell-specific determinant, and a similar dissociation occurs in different cell compartments of a given animal.

the cellular immune response in animals to a given T-cell specific determinant may be expressed as either MIF production or antigen-induced proliferation, and that these two manifestations may be dissociated in the same animal and may occur in different compartments of the same immune system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular immune response of guinea-pigs immunized with L-tyrosin-azobenzoate.
the study of the cellular basis of the immune response in the guinea-pig.
the cellular immune response of the guinea-pig to a monofunctional hapten, L-tyrosyl–p-azophenylarsonate (Rat).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cellular response to RAT was detectable at 2 weeks after immunization, and that the response was maximal at the 3- to 5-week period.
the cellular immune response is a dynamic process in which the different manifestations of immunity are not necessarily synchronous in time or space.

MIF production and proliferation are both important components of a T cell response to a monofunctional hapten, but that they may occur in different cell populations or in the same population in differing stages of development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellular immune response in the guinea-pig is a complex phenomenon, which may be mediated by a variety of different T cell populations.

the MIF assay is a more sensitive test for the presence of T cells in a given population of lymphoid cells than the proliferation assay, and that the latter is probably a better test of the functional capacity of the T cells.
the MIF response is a more sensitive indicator of cellular immune responsiveness than antigen-induced proliferation of lymph node cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cellular immune response in the guinea-pig can be studied in the peritoneal cavity, and the cellular immune response can be measured using the migration inhibition factor assay.

we have demonstrated that the immune system is not only capable of recognizing a wide range of antigens but can also respond to these antigens in a variety of ways, depending on the specific antigen and the specific immune response.
it is possible for the immune system to respond to a single antigenic determinant in different and even opposite ways.
